classification.detection_reasoning: GBALD is a Bayesian active learning method that uses MC dropout for epistemic uncertainty estimation and BALD-style mutual information scoring. It extends BALD with geometric core-set initialization and representativeness ranking, fitting squarely within the Bayesian AL sub-paradigm. The bayesian field guide explicitly lists GBALD as a canonical method.

pluggable_component.name: select_batch
pluggable_component.signature: select_batch(model, x_unlabeled, x_labeled, batch_size, seed, mc_samples: int = 20, R_0: float = 2000.0, eta: float = 0.9, batch_returns: int = 100) -> List[int]
pluggable_component.description: Per-round acquisition function for GBALD Stage 2. Takes a trained model, the unlabeled pool, the current labeled set, and returns batch_size indices into x_unlabeled. Uses MC dropout (mc_samples stochastic passes) to compute BALD scores, ranks candidates by geometric representativeness (R_0/||x - D_j|| relative to labeled set), and selects the top batch_returns candidates. The eta parameter controls ellipsoid geodesic rescaling strength.

scale_dependent_hyperparameters.name: R_0
scale_dependent_hyperparameters.description: Distance threshold for the geometric probability model p(y|x,theta) = R_0 / ||x - D_j|| for points outside the radius. Calibrated for raw [0, 255] pixel distances on MNIST (flattened images, L2 distance in input space). The value is meaningless for normalized data without rescaling. For input dimension d, a reasonable rescaling would be R_0_scaled = 2000.0 * (data_norm / 707) where 707 is the approximate L2 norm of a random raw MNIST image.
scale_dependent_hyperparameters.paper_section: Section 4.2, Equation (5), Section 7.1 - R_0 = 2.0e+3 for all image datasets
